code.title: Safe Divider Drill
code.description:
A math lab drills guarded division. Read two integers a and b. Inside a try block, print the quotient and the remainder when b is not zero; when b is zero, throw an exception so the catch handler prints the error line.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: a and b.

Output Format:
Quotient: <a / b>
Remainder: <a % b>
or, when b is zero:
Cannot divide by zero

Constraints:
-1000 <= a <= 1000, -100 <= b <= 100

code.title: Error Code Thrower
code.description:
A status reader converts error codes into messages using exceptions. Read one integer code. When the code is 0, print the OK line; any other code is thrown as an int, and the catch handler reports it.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: code.

Output Format:
Status: OK
or, for a nonzero code:
Status: Error <code>

Constraints:
-1000 <= code <= 1000

code.title: Unknown Trouble Catcher
code.description:
A sensor monitor demonstrates the catch-all handler. Read one integer mode. When mode is 0, print the normal line; otherwise throw a double value that no typed handler matches, so only the catch (...) handler can respond.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: mode.

Output Format:
System normal
or, for a nonzero mode:
Unknown exception caught

Constraints:
-100 <= mode <= 100

code.title: Passphrase Door Guard
code.description:
A door lock rejects wrong passphrases by throwing a C-style string message. Read one word. When the word is exactly ATOM, print the unlocked line; otherwise throw the const char* message Wrong passphrase and let the catch(const char*) handler print it.

Input Format:
One line with one word: the passphrase.

Output Format:
Door unlocked
or:
Wrong passphrase

Constraints:
1 <= passphrase length <= 20

code.title: Guarded Letter Lookup
code.description:
A text tool reads characters safely using string::at, which throws std::out_of_range for bad indexes. Read one word and one index. Inside a try block, print the character at that index using s.at(index); the catch handler for out_of_range prints the message carried by the caught exception using what().

Input Format:
One line with a word (single word) and an integer index.

Output Format:
Letter: <character at the index>
or, when the index is outside the word:
Out of range: <message from what()>

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 20, 0 <= index <= 30
code.output3: Out of range: basic_string::at: __n (which is 3) >= this->size() (which is 3)
code.sampleoutput2: Out of range: basic_string::at: __n (which is 9) >= this->size() (which is 4)

code.title: Motor Temperature Guard
code.description:
A plant monitor watches a motor's temperature with exceptions. Read one integer temperature. If it reaches 80 or more, throw runtime_error with the message Motor overheated; the catch handler prints Error: followed by the message from what(). Otherwise the motor is running fine.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: temperature.

Output Format:
Motor running at <temp> degrees
or:
Error: Motor overheated

Constraints:
-100 <= temperature <= 200

code.title: Cash Machine Withdrawal Guard
code.description:
An ATM processes a withdrawal inside a try block. Read the account balance and the withdrawal amount. If the amount exceeds the balance, throw runtime_error with the message Insufficient balance, and the catch handler prints the failure line. Otherwise the withdrawal succeeds and the remaining balance is shown.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: balance and amount.

Output Format:
Withdrawal successful
Remaining balance: <balance - amount>
or:
Withdrawal failed: Insufficient balance

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000, 0 <= amount <= 1000000

code.title: Voting Age Validator
code.description:
A polling booth checks voter eligibility using exceptions. Read the age. If the age is below 18, throw the age value itself as an int; the catch(int) handler prints the rejection line showing the age. Otherwise the person is eligible to vote.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: age.

Output Format:
Eligible to vote
or:
Rejected: age <age> is below 18

Constraints:
0 <= age <= 120

code.title: Exam Marks Validator
code.description:
An exam cell rejects negative marks by throwing a string message. Read the marks. If the marks are negative, throw the string Negative marks not allowed and let the catch(const string&) handler print it. Otherwise the marks are recorded.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: marks.

Output Format:
Marks recorded: <marks>
or:
Negative marks not allowed

Constraints:
-100 <= marks <= 100

code.title: Show Seat Booking Guard
code.description:
A theatre box office guards seat booking with try-catch. Read the seats available and the seats requested. If the requested count exceeds the available seats, throw the requested count as an int; the catch(int) handler prints the failure line. Otherwise the booking is confirmed.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: available and requested.

Output Format:
Booking confirmed: <requested> seats
or:
Booking failed: requested <requested> seats

Constraints:
0 <= available <= 500, 0 <= requested <= 500

code.title: Signal Fault Router
code.description:
A device monitor routes numeric signal codes to typed fault handlers. Read a signal code. Inside one try block: code 1 throws the integer 100; code 2 throws the text disk failure; code 3 throws an unnamed double fault; any other code is healthy. Use three catch handlers written in order — catch(int), catch(const char*) and catch(...) — each printing its own line.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: signal code.

Output Format:
One line, depending on the code:
Integer fault: 100 (code 1)
Text fault: disk failure (code 2)
Unknown fault (code 3)
Signal <code>: all clear (any other code)

Constraints:
0 <= code <= 9

code.title: SalaryGuard Custom Exception
code.description:
The payroll service validates salaries with its own exception type. Define a class SalaryError that derives publicly from std::exception, stores a message and overrides what() to return it. Read one integer salary. Inside a try block: a salary of zero or less throws SalaryError with the message Salary must be positive; a salary above 1000000 throws SalaryError with the message Salary exceeds maximum; otherwise print the acceptance line. The catch(const SalaryError&) handler prints SalaryError: followed by what().

Input Format:
One line with one integer: salary.

Output Format:
Salary accepted: <salary>
or:
SalaryError: <message from what()>

Constraints:
-100000 <= salary <= 2000000

code.title: Payment Rethrow Logger
code.description:
A payment gateway logs failures at a low level and decides at a high level. Write a function processPayment(int amount): inside its own try block it prints Processed: <amount> when the amount is at most 10000, and otherwise throws runtime_error with the message limit exceeded. The function's catch (...) handler prints Log: payment failure recorded and then rethrows the very same exception using a bare throw;. In main, read the amount, call processPayment inside another try block, and its catch(const exception&) handler prints Final status: followed by what().

Input Format:
One line with one integer: amount.

Output Format:
Processed: <amount>
or, on failure, in this order:
Log: payment failure recorded
Final status: limit exceeded

Constraints:
0 <= amount <= 1000000
code.output2:
Log: payment failure recorded
Final status: limit exceeded
code.sampleoutput2:
Log: payment failure recorded
Final status: limit exceeded

code.title: Nested Guard Converter
code.description:
A robot controller nests its guards. Read a mode number and print Mode: <mode> first. Then run an inner try inside an outer try: the inner block prints Steady state when mode is 0, and otherwise throws the mode value. The inner block has only a catch (...) handler, which prints Inner guard: unknown disturbance and converts the trouble by throwing the fixed integer code 9. The outer catch(int) handler then prints Outer handler took code 9.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: mode.

Output Format:
Mode: <mode>
then either:
Steady state
or:
Inner guard: unknown disturbance
Outer handler took code 9

Constraints:
-100 <= mode <= 100
code.output1:
Mode: 1
Inner guard: unknown disturbance
Outer handler took code 9
code.output2:
Mode: 100
Inner guard: unknown disturbance
Outer handler took code 9
code.output3:
Mode: -7
Inner guard: unknown disturbance
Outer handler took code 9
code.sampleoutput2:
Mode: 5
Inner guard: unknown disturbance
Outer handler took code 9

code.title: Mini Command Processor
code.description:
A coding playground runs mini calculator commands. Read N, then process N commands one after another. Each command is a word followed by its numbers:
- div a b: integer division a / b; when b is 0 the command throws runtime_error with the message divide by zero
- sqrt x: the integer square root of x (the largest whole number r with r * r <= x); when x is negative the command throws runtime_error with the message negative input
- any other command word throws runtime_error with the message unknown command
Wrap the processing of each command in its own try-catch so one failure never stops the rest. Print one line per command.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N, the number of commands.
Next N lines: one command per line. Invalid command words appear alone, with no numbers after them.

Output Format:
N lines, each either:
Result: <value>
or:
Error: <message from what()>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20; div: 0 <= a <= 1000000, 0 <= b <= 1000; sqrt: -1000 <= x <= 100000
code.output2:
Result: 0
Result: 3
Error: divide by zero
code.output3:
Error: unknown command
Error: negative input
code.whitelist: try, catch, throw, runtime_error, string, cin, cout
code.sampleoutput1:
Result: 5
Result: 4
Error: divide by zero
code.sampleoutput2:
Result: 0
Result: 2
Error: unknown command
Error: negative input

code.title: Bank Transfer Validator
code.description:
A banking backend validates transfers with two custom exception classes, both deriving from std::exception and overriding what(): InvalidAccount (message Invalid account number) and InsufficientFunds (message Insufficient funds). Read the balance, the account number and the amount. Inside a try block: an account outside 100000 to 999999 throws InvalidAccount; an amount greater than the balance throws InsufficientFunds; otherwise print the success line. Catch each exception type in its own handler, each printing Transfer failed: followed by what().

Input Format:
One line with three integers: balance, account, amount.

Output Format:
Transfer of <amount> to account <account> completed
or:
Transfer failed: Invalid account number
or:
Transfer failed: Insufficient funds

Constraints:
0 <= balance <= 1000000, 0 <= account <= 2000000, 0 <= amount <= 1000000
code.whitelist: class, exception, what, try, catch, throw

code.title: Mutex Range Summer
code.description:
A performance lab builds a shared counter protected by a mutex. Read three limits a, b and c. Launch three threads: thread 1 adds the numbers 1 to a, thread 2 adds 1 to b and thread 3 adds 1 to c. Every thread first computes its own partial sum into its own slot, then adds that partial sum to the shared total while holding a mutex with lock_guard. Join all three threads, and only after joining print each partial sum and the shared total.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: a, b and c.

Output Format:
Thread 1 sum: <1 + 2 + ... + a>
Thread 2 sum: <1 + 2 + ... + b>
Thread 3 sum: <1 + 2 + ... + c>
Total: <sum of the three partial sums>

Constraints:
0 <= a, b, c <= 1000

Thread 2 sum: 1
Thread 3 sum: 1
Total: 3

Thread 2 sum: 500500
Thread 3 sum: 500500
Total: 1501500

Thread 1 sum: 0

Thread 1 sum: 6
Thread 2 sum: 10
Thread 3 sum: 15
Total: 31
code.sampleoutput2:

Thread 3 sum: 465

code.title: Parallel Array Sum Split
code.description:
A big array is split between two worker threads. Read N and then N integers. Thread A sums the first half (indices 0 to N/2 - 1) and thread B sums the second half (indices N/2 to N-1); each writes its result into its own slot. Join both threads, and only after joining print the two partial sums and the grand total.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
First half: <sum of the first half>
Second half: <sum of the second half>
Total: <sum of all elements>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, -100000 <= element <= 100000

code.title: Transaction Hub Error Hierarchy
code.description:
A transaction hub routes operations through one processor function that throws typed errors. Build an exception hierarchy: a base class AppError deriving from std::exception that stores a message and overrides what(); class PaymentError deriving from AppError; class NetworkError deriving from AppError. The processor handles one integer code per transaction:
- code 0 returns the text OK
- code 1 throws PaymentError with the message payment declined
- code 2 throws NetworkError with the message network timeout
- any other code throws AppError with the message unknown code
Read N and then N codes. For every transaction print one status line, catching the derived types before the base type.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N.
Line 2: N integer codes separated by spaces.

Output Format:
N lines, each either:
Op<i> OK
or:
Op<i> PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
or:
Op<i> NETWORK-FAIL network timeout
or:
Op<i> APP-FAIL unknown code
where i is the 1-based transaction number.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, -100 <= code <= 100
code.output1:
Op1 PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
Op2 PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
Op3 PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
code.output2:
Op1 NETWORK-FAIL network timeout
Op2 OK
Op3 APP-FAIL unknown code
Op4 PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
Op5 NETWORK-FAIL network timeout
code.whitelist: class, exception, what, try, catch, throw
code.sampleoutput1:
Op1 OK
Op2 PAYMENT-FAIL payment declined
Op3 NETWORK-FAIL network timeout
Op4 APP-FAIL unknown code

code.title: Synchronized Ticket Sellers
code.description:
A cinema box office runs three seller threads against one shared stock. Read the opening stock S and the share each seller must sell: s1, s2 and s3 (their sum never exceeds S). Each seller thread sells exactly its share one ticket at a time, locking a mutex with lock_guard for every single decrement of the shared stock, and counts its own sales into its own slot. Join all three threads, and only after joining print the per-seller sales and the remaining stock.

Input Format:
One line with four integers: S, s1, s2 and s3.

Output Format:
Seller 1 sold: <s1>
Seller 2 sold: <s2>
Seller 3 sold: <s3>
Remaining stock: <S - s1 - s2 - s3>

Constraints:
3 <= S <= 100000, 1 <= s1, s2, s3 <= 1000, s1 + s2 + s3 <= S

Seller 1 sold: 1
Seller 2 sold: 2
Seller 3 sold: 3
Remaining stock: 4

Seller 2 sold: 400
Seller 3 sold: 100
Remaining stock: 0
code.output3:
Seller 1 sold: 1000
Seller 2 sold: 1000
Seller 3 sold: 1000
Remaining stock: 97000

Seller 1 sold: 30
Seller 2 sold: 20
Seller 3 sold: 10
Remaining stock: 40
code.sampleoutput2:
Seller 1 sold: 20
Seller 2 sold: 20
Seller 3 sold: 20

mcqs.title: Role of the try Block
mcqs.description: In a C++ try-catch arrangement, what is the role of the try block?
mcqs.Option1: It silently ignores every error inside it
mcqs.Option2: It encloses code whose exceptions can be handled by the catch handlers that follow it
mcqs.Option4: It stops the program at the first statement

mcqs.title: Job of the throw Statement
mcqs.description: What does the throw statement do in C++?
mcqs.Option1: It catches an exception raised earlier
mcqs.Option2: It prints an error message and ends the program gracefully
mcqs.Option3: It signals an exception, transferring control to the nearest matching catch handler
mcqs.Option4: It converts an exception into a return code

mcqs.title: Meaning of catch(...)
mcqs.description: What does the catch (...) handler with an ellipsis do?
mcqs.Option2: It catches exceptions thrown only from main()
mcqs.Option3: It prevents exceptions from ever being thrown
mcqs.Option4: It catches an exception of any type

mcqs.title: Purpose of what()
mcqs.description: The what() member function of std::exception is used to:
mcqs.Option1: Get a C-style string that describes the exception
mcqs.Option2: Get the line number where the error happened
mcqs.Option3: Get the runtime type of the exception
mcqs.Option4: Clear the exception state of the program

mcqs.title: What Is a Thread
mcqs.description: Which statement best describes a thread in C++?
mcqs.Option1: A separate process with its own address space
mcqs.Option2: The smallest unit of execution that runs concurrently inside a process and shares the process address space
mcqs.Option3: A compiled library loaded at runtime
mcqs.Option4: A special kind of loop that repeats itself

mcqs.title: What thread join() Does
mcqs.description: What happens when the main thread calls t1.join() on a std::thread object t1?
mcqs.Option2: The results of t1 are copied back to the caller
mcqs.Option3: The calling thread blocks until t1 finishes its execution
mcqs.Option4: Thread t1 is paused for one second

mcqs.title: Purpose of a Mutex
mcqs.description: Why is a mutex used in multithreaded C++ programs?
mcqs.Option1: To make every thread run faster
mcqs.Option2: To ensure only one thread at a time can access the shared resource it protects
mcqs.Option4: To print messages from many threads safely

mcqs.title: Uncaught Exception Outcome
mcqs.description: If an exception is thrown but no catch handler anywhere accepts it, what happens?
mcqs.Option1: The program ignores the exception and continues
mcqs.Option2: The exception is printed and execution resumes normally
mcqs.Option3: The runtime calls std::terminate and the program aborts
mcqs.Option4: The exception is converted into a compiler warning

mcqs.title: Header Needed for std::thread
mcqs.description: Which header must be included to create threads with std::thread?
mcqs.Option2: <mutex>
mcqs.Option4: <thread>

mcqs.title: Base Class of Standard Exceptions
mcqs.description: All standard C++ exception classes (such as std::runtime_error and std::out_of_range) inherit from which class?
mcqs.Option2: std::error
mcqs.Option4: std::throwable

mcqs.title: Int Handler Beats Catch-All
mcqs.description: What does this program print?
mcqs.Option2: int handler catch-all handler
mcqs.Option4: Compile error

mcqs.title: Custom Exception Message via what()
mcqs.description: What does this program print?
mcqs.Option2: Denied: LowBalance
mcqs.Option4: Compile error

mcqs.title: No Double to Int Handler Match
mcqs.description: What does this program print?
mcqs.Option2: generic handler
mcqs.Option4: No output

mcqs.title: Inner Catch Converts for Outer
mcqs.description: What does this program print?
mcqs.Option2: inner caught converted
mcqs.Option4: Compile error

mcqs.title: Stack Unwinding Meaning
mcqs.description: In C++, what does stack unwinding refer to when an exception is thrown?
mcqs.Option1: The program restarts execution from the first line of main
mcqs.Option2: Every function on the call stack is called again in reverse order
mcqs.Option3: As the call stack is searched for a matching handler, local objects in each exited scope are destroyed in reverse order
mcqs.Option4: The stack memory is released without calling any destructors

mcqs.title: Why Catch by const Reference
mcqs.description: Why is catching exceptions by const reference, as in catch (const MyError& e), the recommended style?
mcqs.Option1: It is the only syntax the standard allows for user-defined exceptions
mcqs.Option2: It makes the exception travel faster through the stack
mcqs.Option3: References never bind to temporaries, so bad throws are rejected at compile time
mcqs.Option4: It avoids object slicing and unnecessary copies while preserving polymorphic behaviour

mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.Option4: caught inner boom outer caught outer boom

mcqs.title: Bare Rethrow Keeps Original
mcqs.description: What does this program print?

mcqs.Option4: logged bad code bad code

mcqs.title: What Is a Data Race
mcqs.description: What is a data race in a multithreaded C++ program?
mcqs.Option1: Two threads finishing their work at different speeds
mcqs.Option2: Two threads using two different mutexes for the same data
mcqs.Option3: Two threads accessing the same memory location concurrently without synchronization, at least one of them writing, which makes the result undefined
mcqs.Option4: A thread that finishes before join() is called on it
